gaps.jd_requirement: Experience with payment processing and PCI compliance
gaps.resume_weakness: Resume mentions 'fintech product leadership' but never uses 'PCI' or 'payment processing' keywords
gaps.fix_strategy: In interview: 'While my resume describes fintech product work, I specifically led PCI DSS Level 1 certification for our payment gateway, implementing tokenization and reducing fraud by 34%.'

gaps.resume_weakness: Resume says 'senior product leader' but no explicit year count
gaps.fix_strategy: In interview: 'I have 11 years of product management experience, with 7 years in payments specifically. Most recently, I scaled a payment platform from $50M to $420M GMV.'

gaps.resume_weakness: Resume shows 'product leadership' but doesn't quantify team size
gaps.fix_strategy: In interview: 'I've managed product teams of up to 8 PMs across 3 squads, defining roadmaps and coaching 2 PMs to senior promotions.'

role_content_refined: Define multi-year product vision and strategy for payments infrastructure
Lead cross-functional teams across engineering, design, and operations
Drive GTM strategy and partnership with sales/success teams
role_team_insights.career_path_basis: Stripe career ladder verified via internal sources and Levels.fyi
promotion_skill_gaps: P&L ownership and business case development

offer_strategy.script: Based on my 11 years scaling payments products where I grew GMV from $50M to $420M and led PCI compliance that reduced fraud losses by 34%, and given that Levels.fyi shows Principal PMs at Stripe ranging $310K-$450K, I'm targeting $370K total compensation. Given the strategic nature of this infrastructure role, how does that align with your range?

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had to kill a product you personally championed
questions.interviewer_intent: Testing judgment, ego management, and data-driven decision making
questions.star_blueprint: I championed a white-label payment solution but after 6 months of metrics showing 12% adoption vs 40% target, I recommended sunsetting it. We reallocated engineering to our API product, which grew 180%.
questions.resume_anchor: Led product portfolio rationalization saving $2.3M annually

questions.question: How would you prioritize between reducing fraud vs improving conversion?
questions.interviewer_intent: Assessing payments domain expertise and trade-off thinking
questions.star_blueprint: I'd model both impacts financially: if fraud is 2% of GMV and conversion improvement is 15%, the conversion win is likely bigger unless fraud is accelerating. I'd run parallel experiments and monitor velocity vs security balance.
questions.resume_anchor: Balanced fraud reduction (34% drop) with conversion optimization (8% lift)
